## Recommendation

### Recommend whether to launch and explain uncertainty.

Launch is financially attractive under the supplied incremental scenario, with $4,000 contribution after the new campaign cost. The forecast is 600 incremental units, not observed orders; the listed 1,000-unit capacity can accommodate that forecast. Proceed conditionally on validating incremental demand and confirming that the quoted price, variable cost and one-time campaign cost apply. Do not describe the forecast result as a realized profit or unconditional approval. `ECON901/Week 02 - Oct 12/launch-case.md`

At the supplied $20 contribution per unit, 400 units cover the campaign cost. Below that volume the scenario loses money; at 400 units it breaks even. The earlier $3,000 research expenditure is unrecoverable and therefore excluded from this incremental decision, not erased from historical spending. Other case parts remain background to this Part 2 response. `ECON901/Assignments/launch.md` `ECON901/Week 02 - Oct 12/launch-case.md`

## Computations

### Calculate incremental launch profit using the supplied scenario.

These five calculations were executed with the CLI calculator and checked against the supplied case inputs. The supplied quantities are forecast units 600, price $50, variable cost $30 per unit and new fixed campaign cost $8,000. Derived revenue, cost and unit contribution are carried into the profit and break-even computations; no tax, cannibalization, financing or opportunity-cost adjustment is invented. `ECON901/Week 02 - Oct 12/launch-case.md`

### Incremental launch scenario

| Measure | Executed calculation | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Forecast revenue | 600 × 50 | $30,000 |
| Forecast variable cost | 600 × 30 | $18,000 |
| Contribution per unit | 50 − 30 | $20 |
| Incremental launch profit | 30,000 − 18,000 − 8,000 | $4,000 |
| Break-even units | 8,000 ÷ 20 | 400 |

The profit above is a scenario contribution after the new campaign, not a complete after-tax or discounted accounting-profit measure. The sunk research cost is not an incremental launch expense. `ECON901/Week 02 - Oct 12/launch-case.md`

## Limitations

PENDING — requires observed incremental orders or a supported demand study before treating the 600-unit forecast as verified demand. These are absent from the case; they are not assumed to be zero. `ECON901/Week 02 - Oct 12/launch-case.md`
